overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by convening in executive session on May 11 without a roll call vote, but found the Purpose 6 executive session proper; it also recommended amending the minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board convened in executive session on May 11 for an improper purpose, since negotiation strategy was premature for the 59 Water Street property.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it convened in executive session on May 11 to discuss matters related to the sale and value of 59 Water Street.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to vote by roll call to convene in executive session on May 11; the Board acknowledged no roll call vote was taken.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law when it failed to vote to convene in executive session on May 11.

allegations.summary: Not alleged in the complaint: the May 11 open session minutes recorded a motion and roll call vote to convene in executive session that did not occur. The AG addressed it.
allegations.key_passage: Meeting minutes must accurately reflect what actually occurred during a meeting; therefore, it is improper to include in the minutes of the May 11 open session a motion and vote that did not occur.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
